claim: The Wiener Riesenrad opens daily 09:00–23:45, standing nearly 65m tall with a 61m diameter, erected 1897 for Emperor Franz Joseph's 50th throne jubilee; standard ticket is €14.50 with Vienna City Card discount.
quote: Daily, 09:00 - 23:45 ... Standard admission costs €14.50 ... erected in 1897 to commemorate Emperor Franz Joseph's 50th year on the throne ... nearly 65 meters tall with a diameter of approximately 61 meters

claim: Wurstelprater rides typically run 11:00–23:00 (some until midnight or later weekends) during the main season March 15–October 31; in low season the Ferris Wheel still runs 10:00–22:00 while many rides close.
quote: Main Season (March 15 – October 31): Rides & stands: usually from 11:00 am to 11:00 pm, some until midnight or even later on weekends; Giant Ferris Wheel: 9:00 am – 11:45 pm ... Low Season: many rides close, but the Ferris Wheel runs daily

claim: A private candlelight dinner in a Riesenrad cabin runs ~90 minutes with a 3-course menu, sparkling wine and wine pairing, priced around €507 for two and requiring booking 6–8 weeks ahead.
quote: candlelight dinner for 2 people costs €507.00 including VAT ... lasts approximately 90 minutes ... 3-course menu with 1 glass of sparkling wine, wine pairing ... book 6-8 weeks in advance

claim: The Prater divides into the Wurstelprater funfair (free to enter, pay-per-ride, 250+ years old with the 117m Prater Tower among modern attractions) and the Green Prater, a ~6km² recreational area nearly twice the size of Central Park.
quote: The Wurstelprater is over 250 years old ... Prater Tower—the fifth highest chain carousel in the world at 117 meters height. Entry to the Wurstelprater grounds is free ... 6 km² recreational area—nearly twice the size of New York's Central Park

claim: The Prater Hauptallee is a 4.5km boulevard popular with joggers and cyclists, reachable via tram line 1 from Schwedenplatz; locals use the skate park and sports meadows while tourists cluster around the Riesenrad and amusement rides.
quote: The Prater Hauptallee is a 4.5km boulevard running through much of the area, described as 'popular with joggers and cyclists.' Visitors can access it via Tram line 1 ... Locals use 'the skate park, sports meadows and other facilities,' while tourists gravitate toward concentrated entertainment

claim: Tourists tend to equate the Prater with the Ferris wheel, while Viennese above all value the 4.5km tree-lined main avenue and the green expanse for foot, bike, boat or horseback exploration.
quote: for many tourists the Prater is essentially synonymous with a Ferris wheel or amusement park, for many Viennese it is above all a beautiful, huge green area with a 4.5 km long main avenue

claim: Bitzinger's Würstelstand at the foot of the Riesenrad has run the Prater sausage stands since 2009, opens 10:00–01:00 Mon–Wed/Sun and 10:00–04:00 Thu–Sat, serving classic Käsekrainer, Burenwurst and Bosna with a view of the wheel and Kaiserwiese.
quote: Bitzinger has managed the sausage stands at the Riesenrad ... since 2009 ... Monday-Wednesday and Sunday from 10:00–01:00, and Thursday-Saturday from 10:00–04:00 ... view of the Giant Ferris Wheel and the Kaiserwiese

claim: The Riesenrad is reachable in five minutes from Praterstern (U1/U2) under the railway arches, or directly via tram lines O and 5; budget about two hours for the wheel plus a Schweizerhaus beer.
quote: U-Bahn line U1 or U2 to Praterstern, then take a five-minute walk south under the railway arches. Alternatively, tram O and 5 stop right outside the Riesenrad ... Budget two leisurely hours for the Riesenrad plus a Schweizerhaus beer

claim: Praterstraße in Leopoldstadt has regained colour since cafés like Café Balthasar and Supersense at Dogenhof moved in, making the Danube Canal–to–Prater walk via Nestroyplatz a legitimate alternative approach to the wheel.
quote: Until about 15 years ago, hardly anyone would have set foot into Praterstrasse, but since quirky cafés and shops like Café Balthasar and Supersense at Dogenhof moved in, the area regained its former colour and vibrancy ... walk begins from the Danube Canal to the Prater through Leopoldstadt on Praterstraße

claim: Since May 2022 the Riesenrad also offers Platform No. 9, a glass-bottomed, wall- and roof-less steel platform attachment for thrill-seeking elevated photos.
quote: Since May 2022, thrill-seekers can experience 'Platform No. 9'—a glass-bottomed steel platform with no walls or roof—for an adrenaline-filled height experience
